Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab (DCS), or the Danish Cardiological Society, is a professional medical organization that serves as the foundational anchor for the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK) [^src1]. Through this structural role, DCS plays a central part in ensuring high treatment quality and coordinating a unified national effort for patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation [^src1]. 

The AFDK is a nationwide clinical quality database and development program operating under the broader umbrella of the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program (RKKP) [^src2]. Its mission is to guarantee uniform, evidence-based, and patient-centered care for a frequent and potentially severe chronic heart condition [^src2]. As the professional home for this database, Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab provides the necessary clinical governance and specialist oversight for AFDK's quality indicators and improvement initiatives [^src2]. Furthermore, the database operates with formal approval from the Danish Health Data Authority (Sundhedsdatastyrelsen), solidifying its role in the national healthcare infrastructure alongside these key organizational stakeholders [^src3].
